messages:
mia: Quick triage: after PTQ bring-up for ranky3b-v2 we see ndcg@10 +1.8% but mrr@10 -3.2% on the prod-like holdout, concentrated in the short-query cohort. Uploaded eval outputs and sample ids. Should we pause the rollout?
raj: Paste the exact eval command/flags you ran (seed, dedupe, holdout).
mia: `./eval.py --model ranky3b-v2-ptq --holdout recent30k --cohort short_queries --metrics ndcg@10 mrr@10 --seed 42 --dedupe true`
lina: ndcg up + mrr down often means top1 swaps. ndcg looks deeper into the list; mrr is very top1-sensitive. Short queries magnify this. Check topk diffs and tie-break stability.
ash: saw a similar signature in an earlier 4-bit batch. Tokenization/truncation differences occasionally produced shorter snippet candidates that floated to #1.
yuki: Can we diff top1 between baseline and PTQ for the changed queries? If you dump the two JSONs I can run the diff script.
mia: Quick stats: 1,230 queries with top1 change; 78% of those queries have length <20 chars. In that changed set ndcg increased while mrr decreased; precision@1 falls ~4.1%. s3://redwood-eval/6087654321/top1_changes.json
raj: Verify the harness used the same tokenizer/vocab across baseline and PTQ. PTQ CI sometimes swaps preprocessing container versions by mistake.
lina: Also confirm candidate normalization and dedupe hash parity. `--dedupe true` is ambiguous unless we pin the hash version. Which hash you used?
mia: We used `norm_hash_v2` (lowercase, strip html, collapse whitespace). The PTQ runner used a separate container image though, so mismatch is possible.
nash: Run ndcg@1 and mrr@1 to isolate top1-only signal. If mrr@1 drops and ndcg@10 rises, it's almost certainly top1 flips.
yuki: Suggest sampling 50 top1-swap queries and do manual relevance checks on them. If new top1s are shorter snippets or boilerplate, that's telling.
mia: I'm pulling 50 samples and will post manual labels in ~2h.
deploy-bot: Canary paused (reason: evaluation anomaly detected)
raj: Block rollout until triage done. Action list: 1) tokenizer parity, 2) candidate norm + dedupe parity, 3) tie-break determinism (stable sort + seed), 4) rerun with multiple seeds (42, 123, 7).
lina: I'll own tokenizer + preprocessing parity. raj you take dedupe/tie-break. mia keep evidence and collect manual labels.
mia: Created ticket RERANK-4873 with eval artifacts and failing query ids. Rerunning eval with tokenizer pinned to baseline and `--dedupe false` to isolate. Will post updated metrics (ndcg@10, mrr@10, mrr@1, ndcg@1) when done.
raj: Also run an ablation: remove prompt priming/length tokens from inputs; priming can change ranking behaviour after quantization.
nash: If it's a pure ranking permutation (not a quality drop), we can consider a short-query guard to preserve top1 ordering until we fix the pipeline. But don't deploy heuristics before root cause is understood.
yuki: Ping me once artifacts are up; I can run quick pairwise diffs and a deterministic tie-break audit.
mia: Will do. For now rollout blocked, triage owners assigned, samples and eval commands in the ticket. :thumbsup:
